# Firestore queries and indexes

## Change a serving query

Add or update a runtime query driver in `backend/tests/support/firestore_query_driver_registry.py`; use named caller witnesses when serving helpers are called from routes or services. Drivers execute the real builder against `RecordingFirestore` across its argument profiles. The guard requires every serving shape to be classified, certain, and served by the generated manifest. A failure reports the driver/profile, query shape, and candidate index. Fix the query shape or declare its required index in the same PR. Run `backend/tests/unit/test_firestore_query_shapes.py` and `backend/tests/unit/test_firestore_outside_query_contract.py`.

The backend unit selector includes the Firestore index guard set for every Python source file in the serving-query inventory, including router and helper changes, plus changes to `firestore.indexes.json`, the index registry, and Firestore guard support files. The canonical `firestore-index-guard` manifest check reuses that selector in both local preflight and Release Eligibility, runs only the seven guard files through `backend/test.sh` in a pinned Python environment, and blocks proof for a failing main SHA even if `Backend unit suite` was merged over. Environment/setup errors fail closed with a separate diagnostic; restore the guard environment and rerun rather than skipping it. `Backend unit suite` is not currently a required branch-protection check. The release check is diff-scoped: a later unrelated SHA can receive proof without rerunning it, and explicit `skip_eligibility_proof` break-glass remains an operator bypass.

`GET /v1/conversations` and `/v1/conversations/count` reject multiple sources combined with multiple statuses and cap each list at 20 (`MAX_IN_FILTER_VALUES`), so the Firestore disjunction limit is not reachable through these routes.

## Declare an index

Edit `backend/database/firestore_index_registry.py`, then run:

```bash
backend/.venv/bin/python backend/scripts/generate_firestore_indexes.py --write
```

Commit the registry and generated `firestore.indexes.json` together. Do not hand-edit the generated manifest or create undeclared indexes directly in a project. Single-field collection-group requirements are field requirements in the registry and generated `fieldOverrides`; an oracle `create_exemption=` suggestion belongs on this path, not in a composite query spec.

## Apply and deploy

Merging a manifest PR triggers `.github/workflows/gcp_firestore_indexes.yml`. Development applies automatically; production validates locally and stays pending until the release owner dispatches main for cumulative reconciliation, approves its run, and observes source-pinned READY (R15 step 0). Every backend-source image shipment — deploy, job, or Helm upgrade — passes the shared `.github/actions/firestore-readiness` composite first. Each caller stages the gate controls from its own immutable `github.workflow_sha` into .github/firestore-workflow after the runtime-source checkout, then the composite checks out the exact admitted `source_sha`, verifies its `firestore.indexes.json` was generated by that commit's registry (a pre-registry commit's checked-in manifest is validated structurally instead), and `--check-only`s `vars.RUNTIME_GCP_PROJECT_ID` on the `(default)` database authenticated keylessly through the calling job's `omi-gha-deploy-prod`/`omi-gha-deploy-dev` workload identity provider as `omi-ci-index-check@based-hardware.iam.gserviceaccount.com` (custom role `ciFirestoreIndexReader`, granted in both `based-hardware` and `based-hardware-dev`; impersonable from both deploy pools via `attribute.repository_id/776121034`) in an isolated `CLOUDSDK_CONFIG`, so deploy credentials can never win and no JSON key exists to leak. JIT QA lanes target `env.QA_PROJECT`/`env.QA_FIRESTORE_DATABASE`. `gcp_backend_listen_helm.yml` gates only its explicit-tag path: kept-tag and rollback lanes replay an image already served in the same environment and the index pipeline is create-only, so the shared gate is conditioned on `env.BACKEND_LISTEN_SOURCE_SHA != ''` and rollback gains no new failure mode. The sync-ledger cutover consumes an operator-supplied backend image (nominal contract: only images published by the gated builders `gcp_backend.yml`/`gcp_backend_auto_dev.yml`; the workflow's generic `@sha256` digest check does not enforce the repository) and never builds one, so it runs no gate of its own. A failed gate blocks the shipment and uploads a locally revalidated, short-TTL proposal artifact for the apply lane. Schedule the production approval and index build before a backend release that depends on the new index. Reconciliation creates missing composites and union-preserving field indexes; destructive `indexes=[]` exemptions use the separate confirmed `field-exemptions` operation. Deploy workflows never mutate the serving schema.

`web/admin` has a separate TypeScript query contract at `web/admin/lib/__tests__/firestore-query-contract.test.ts`, run by `web-checks.yml` for changes under `web/admin/**` and `firestore.indexes.json`. `web/personas-open-source` queries Firestore client-side and is outside the Python guard; its only composite shapes (`messages`: `pluginId ASC, timestamp ASC` and `botName ASC, timestamp ASC`) are declared in the registry and READY in prod (verified 2026-10-01); its Firebase project is build-time configurable.

The real-Firestore oracle is `backend/scripts/firestore_index_oracle.py`. Use it when validating a query/index change against Firestore's actual planning response or investigating a suspected index gap. It is an oracle and does not provision indexes.

## Budget a new queue, job or lease collection

A new Firestore collection that stores queue, job, lease, dispatch, retry, progress or recovery state must declare a read budget in `.github/firestore-collection-budgets.json` in the same PR that introduces it. The batch pipeline's job/queue/lease collections reached ~1.36B of ~1.83B reads/day before anyone wrote the number down, so the number is now a merge-time requirement rather than a post-incident discovery.

`firestore-collection-budget` (`.github/scripts/check_firestore_collection_budget.py`) is diff-scoped: a collection or computed site that already exists at the merge base is grandfathered, and only a name that first appears in the change needs an entry. It scans both in-repo Firestore surfaces: Python under `backend/` (`.collection()`, `.collection_group()`) and TypeScript/JavaScript under `web/` (`db.collection()`, `db.collectionGroup()`, `collection(db, ...)`, `doc(db, ...)`). A `budgets` entry names the owning lane, the unit of work, `reads_per_unit_budget`, `reads_per_day_budget`, `basis` (`measured` or `planning-bound`), the source of the number, and the review date. A `planning-bound` entry is an estimate and is never booked as a saving.

A **computed** collection name — `client.collection(f'new_{stage}_jobs')`, `db.collection(collectionName)`, a template literal whose collection segment is interpolated — cannot be resolved statically, so it fails closed. Declare it in the registry's `dynamic` list with the `site`, the `expression` exactly as the guard prints it, the `collection_pattern` family, and the same budget fields; the family budget then covers every member the expression can produce. A path whose collection segments are static (`f'users/{uid}/jobs'`) resolves normally and only the new `jobs` collection needs a budget. If the token heuristic misclassifies a name or a site, add it to `exempt` with a reason instead of inventing a budget.

A grandfathered computed site keeps its `site::expression` key when the literal namespace tuple it reads gains a member — `NAMESPACES = ('batch_pipeline_prod', 'batch_pipeline_dev')` becoming `('batch_pipeline_prod', 'batch_pipeline_dev', 'batch_pipeline_preview')` — so the key-level check cannot see the new collection. When the guard can enumerate the family from a literal tuple or list (a `for` loop or an assignment such as `namespace = NAMESPACES[index]` in the same file), a member that first appears in the change needs its own `budgets` entry or an `exempt` entry: the family budget was reviewed against the old membership, and a new namespace is a new read surface.

The guard is a disclosure ratchet, not semantic analysis: a name assembled from config or a runtime registry is invisible, and only families the guard can enumerate from literal sequences are compared between revisions. `FIRESTORE_COLLECTION_BUDGET_GUARD_ENABLED=0` disables it for an approved rollback and requires `FIRESTORE_COLLECTION_BUDGET_GUARD_DISABLE_REASON` so the disable is visible in the run log.

## Respond to a missing-index alert

Historic composite qualification: only the `batch_pipeline_dev_jobs` and
`batch_pipeline_prod_jobs` COLLECTION signatures with `state ASCENDING,
enqueued_at ASCENDING` may match the Admin API form with a terminal
`__name__ ASCENDING`. Both forms retain exact project/database/collection
resource identity and `ANY_API` scope. Multiple matching resources remain
ambiguous; CREATING, missing and every other non-READY state still block.
This compatibility does not extend to new collections, fields, directions or
query scopes. It is shared by check-only, wait and missing-index qualification;
it does not change declarations, provision indexes, or establish readiness by
itself. Workflow controls still qualify the admitted application source rather
than changing its pin.

The backend provisions a missing-index alert through `.github/scripts/ensure_firestore_missing_index_alert.py`. Follow `backend/docs/runbooks/firestore-missing-index.md`: confirm the actual query and platform suggestion, declare the composite or collection-group field requirement in the registry, regenerate the manifest, and verify the request after readiness. Never copy a suggested index directly into a project.

## Validate declarations without occupying the writer queue

Same-repository PRs against main run the credential-free additive manifest
plan, using immutable trusted main controls and candidate JSON as data. Pushes
to main validate the generated manifest locally. Neither path calls GCP,
receives cloud credentials, or occupies schema writer concurrency. A green
validation check does not establish production readiness. The push summary
records `SCHEMA_PENDING`, exact source SHA, the release owner role and a UTC
deadline two hours after the check. The owner must arrange readiness before a
dependent shipment, including when a check finishes after the release target.

The release owner dispatches the existing composite operation on `main`,
supplies `APPLY_FIRESTORE_INDEXES`, approves only its owned
production run and verifies all named indexes READY before deployment (R15
step 0). The composite and destructive field-exemption jobs share the same
noncancelling `firestore-schema-prod` job lock. Field exemptions retain their
separate typed confirmation and production-only approval. Automatic and manual
development composite writers share `firestore-schema-development`.

Dispatch reconciliation is cumulative and pinned to the immutable main SHA
selected by that run, not to an older `SCHEMA_PENDING` receipt. If main advances,
the writer deliberately uses the newer tip's manifest, registry and controls.
`SCHEMA_SOURCE` records the actual dispatch source and operation after checkout
identity verification. There is no historical source-SHA dispatch input. The
owner must retain the older pending source and separately prove its named
indexes, plus those of the dependent release source, READY using the existing
source-pinned readiness gate. A successful newer writer alone cannot close an
older receipt: declarations might have changed or been removed. Missing or
ambiguous readiness evidence leaves it pending. This changes neither matcher
qualification nor the release's source admission.

Read-only push/PR jobs cannot displace a pending writer. GitHub concurrency
still retains only one pending writer and does not guarantee FIFO ordering;
release owners must recheck their exact run rather than assuming every dispatch
will finish. Do not cancel an active mutation to prove scheduling. On a later
normally admitted run, prove the pinned dispatch starts despite pending local
checks, writers never overlap, and named indexes are READY. Existing deploy
readiness checks and schema timeouts are unchanged.

This scheduling change does not qualify historic implicit `__name__` aliases
or change index matching, apiScope/resource identity or ambiguity rules. Those
remain separate schema/readiness review decisions.
